exclude_always: llm, which is covered by model confirmation, not the sweep

exclude_conditionally.rerank_candidates_and_reranker: Counted in A's denominator ONLY if the rerank axis trial showed rerank=true beating the noise floor, so rerank is kept in the current best. If rerank is not kept, both sub-axes are excluded from the denominator and recorded as 'not applicable (rerank not kept)', not as not-tested.
exclude_conditionally.struck_at_reconnaissance: Any parameter axis struck at reconnaissance with recorded evidence, for example template when GET /v1/prompt-templates returns only one template, or query_rewrite when the resolved QueryRequest schema exposes no rewrite field.
exclude_conditionally.use_graph: A graph-not-attributable finding under decision_ledger rev 5 d_graph_scope COUNTS AS a reconnaissance strike of use_graph for that collection. It is excluded from A's denominator and recorded as not-tested (graph not attributable), never as no-effect.

B_denominator.exclusions: Structures struck at reconnaissance by the feasibility rule in d_structure_orchestration, with evidence.

modifiers_not_in_B.chunk_neighbourhood_expansion: Optional modifier. May be tried once on the final phase-B winner if budget remains. Its result is reported, but it is excluded from B's denominator and numerator.
modifiers_not_in_B.prompt_arm_mutation: A modifier used inside other structures. It is never scored as a standalone structure and is excluded from B.
modifiers_not_in_B.table_fill: Excluded from B. Scored separately, only on the enumerative subset of benchmark questions, if the benchmark contains at least 5 enumerative questions and budget remains. Its result is reported in the structure comparison with its subset size and never mixed into the main structure ranking.

structure_notes.graph_seeded: Struck automatically on graph-not-attributable collections, per d_graph_scope. It is in B only where the graph is attributable.
structure_notes.single_shot: Always in B. It is the control arm, so the denominator is never 0.

rule.reporting: The coverage record lists, per collection: every axis and structure, whether it is in the denominator, whether it was covered, and the reason for any exclusion. This lets anyone recompute c from the record.
rule.why: These fixed denominators make A, B and c reproducible across valid designs. A value of 1.0 then means exactly that every applicable parameter axis and every feasible standalone structure was scored.

rule.denominator: Root progress N is the number of readable ASM collections confirmed at reconnaissance. The expected value is 3.
rule.mismatch: If reconnaissance finds a count other than 3: record the discrepancy and the identifiers, proceed with the collections actually readable, and flag the mismatch in the root terminal update and in the cross-collection note. If no readable collection is an ASM paper collection, close as blocked under the safety_policy trigger.

rule.anti_gaming: A structure or axis may be struck only with recorded evidence. Struck counts are reported next to the coverage fractions.
rule.collection_score: c = 0.5 + 0.25 * A + 0.25 * B for a collection WITH a verified result-bearing closure (decision_ledger rev 5 d_credit_result_bearing_only). c = 0 for every other collection.
rule.denominators: A and B are defined exactly by d_coverage_denominators.
rule.reporting: The root terminal update and the root closure summary report c, A, B and the struck counts per collection. Quality scores are never averaged.
rule.root_progress: root_episode_progress = (sum of c over readable ASM collections) / N.
rule.stagnation_compatibility: Root observations are recorded only at verified result-bearing closures. Each adds at least 0.5 / N, so root stagnation cannot fire while collections remain open.

rule.order: Process collections one at a time, largest document count first. Carry each collection to closure, including close-out and holdout scoring, before the next collection's setup begins.
rule.reconnaissance: Cheap reconnaissance for all collections may run up front.
rule.why: Tenant budget exhaustion or a run-wide abort stops everything. Serial processing leaves fully closed, credited results for the collections already done.

rule.cost: Every orchestration call is a tenant billable call and counts in that trial's cost vector and call multiple.
rule.deterministic_glue: Non-LLM steps are plain code in the harness.
rule.feasibility_check: At reconnaissance, run a 3-question smoke test of each multi-call standalone structure's orchestration step through /v1/query. A structure passes if the harness can parse the output deterministically.
rule.infeasible_structure: A structure that fails the smoke test, or that cannot be built without an LLM step outside a tenant /v1/query call, is struck at reconnaissance and recorded as not-tested (infeasible), with evidence. It is excluded from B.
rule.judge_isolation: The Episode's own model never takes part in producing any scored answer.
rule.orchestration_model: Every LLM step inside a multi-call structure (sufficiency assessment, gap follow-up, decomposition, sub-answer synthesis, table-fill frontier updates) is performed by the TENANT through POST /v1/query, on the same cheap sweep model the trial uses, with the collection and all parameters set explicitly. The Episode's own model is never used for orchestration.

blocked_vocabulary_now: any item of the safety_policy human_escalation list, quoted verbatim
rule.on_either: Stop all tenant calls run-wide at once, with no retry and no waiting. Write the resumable checkpoint. Close every unclosed collection, whether in progress or unstarted, as bound_hit and name the bound; never close it as blocked. Credit for an in-progress collection follows d_coverage_weighted_credit. An unstarted collection earns 0. Then proceed to root close-out.
rule.single_status_rule: not_tested applies ONLY to a collection that is unreadable, has zero documents, or was cut by the recorded per-collection allocation at reconnaissance before setup began. bound_hit applies to everything stopped by a bound. blocked applies only to the triggers above. Once benchmark construction has been attempted, fewer than 10 validated synthesis questions closes as bound_hit benchmark_shortfall.

checkpoint_contents: run id, UTC timestamp, and the detection record of the stopping response
per collection: status, phase reached, tenant calls spent per pool, remaining allocation, and c, A and B so far with denominators
hashes of each frozen benchmark, tuning/holdout split and seed, and the judging prompt
noise-floor record, leaderboard so far, named current-best configuration, and the queue of untested axes and structures
resolved model identities (cheap sweep, strong, judge) and the tenant /v1/version
rule.checkpoint_rules: The checkpoint is a file in the run directory, listed in the closure manifest with its hash. It contains no token material and no Authorization header.
rule.resume_is_out_of_scope: Resuming after the Monday reset is a separate, human-approved run that reads this checkpoint. That run first reruns one baseline repeat for each partially complete collection and compares /v1/version and the model identities against the checkpoint. If the baseline falls outside the recorded noise floor, or any version changed, earlier trials are not comparable. The resuming run must then say so, and either re-establish the noise floor or restart that collection's search.

additions: the resumable checkpoint (required whenever a run-wide stop occurred)
per-collection budget record: tenant calls spent per pool against the 1500 ceiling
structure feasibility record: smoke-test evidence and a struck/kept verdict per structure
coverage record per collection, as defined in d_coverage_denominators, including c, A, B and every exclusion reason
root closure summary listing every readable collection with its status, reason, c, A and B
root manifest file: every deliverable path with its SHA-256, written and verified by the root at close-out
rule.rule: The deliverable is decision_ledger rev 5 d_deliverable_manifest AS EXTENDED by the additions. The root verifies the whole extended manifest at close-out.
rule.terminal_update_reference: The root terminal update carries the root manifest's path and SHA-256.

decisions.rule: The operative run end is the root's own terminal update, issued once every readable collection is closed, or a safety bound. stopping.target 1.0 means full applicable coverage of every collection, and is expected to be unreachable when any collection closes as blocked, not_tested or partially covered. The host safety bounds are the backstop.

content.precedence: Operator decisions from the Duet. For the items they cover, they take precedence over decision_ledger rev 5, execution_policy rev 2 and task_specification rev 3. They never loosen safety_policy rev 2.
content.provenance: Operator answers recorded in the Duet: (a) ASM paper text may go to the Episode's own model; (b) if the budget runs out, wait until the Monday reset; (c) there are three ASM collections. Follow-ups: (1) YES, stop-and-checkpoint with a separate resume run; (2) the weekly budget is unknown.

resolved_operator_questions.resolution: Operator confirmed: stop immediately, write the checkpoint, and resume in a separate human-approved run after the Monday reset.

The weekly budget is unknown. Keep the 1500-call per-collection ceiling. Serial largest-first processing, exhaustion detection, the checkpoint, and coverage-weighted credit handle a smaller budget and keep any shortfall visible.
resolved_operator_questions.status: RESOLVED by operator (budget unknown; ceiling kept)
